source.title: Memorization Through the Lens of Curvature of Loss Function Around Samples
source.authors: Isha Garg; Deepak Ravikumar; Kaushik Roy

page_placements.theme: Identifying corrupted supervision depends on the diagnostic and training conditions

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether corrupted training examples are memorized by measuring their curvature and identifying them, but does not reproduce the original random-label training experiment or measure its train/test errors.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover synthetic label corruption and the related 2D noisy-data curvature dynamics. The paper's discussion of fully randomized labels is attributed to Zhang et al. (2017), so it is not extracted as this study's result. The 2D example's loss and curvature dynamics are reported as figures and text, not as numerical row values. Other curvature and memorization comparisons (including FZ-score comparisons) do not measure a claim version's named behavior.
record.test_reason: Section 4.3 explicitly reports 100% training accuracy on MNIST with 1% randomly corrupted labels. This bears narrowly on V4's perfect-training-fit component. The curvature and detection results do not test the claim versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly describes the authors' main conclusion: epoch-averaged input loss curvature is a scalable sample-memorization metric supported by qualitative examples, agreement with FZ scores, and synthetic-label detection. Its categorical claim that no version is directly tested needs qualification: the reported 100% training accuracy at 1% MNIST label corruption bears on V4's training-fit component.
record.recipe_differences: Measures input loss curvature during training and trains on selected synthetic label corruptions; it does not reproduce the original random-label train/test error experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Curvature dynamics vary over training: the toy example's curvature rises early and decreases after overfitting; the authors use epoch-averaged scores for their main analyses. Curvature comparisons also vary with weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Corrupted examples have high curvature, and curvature identifies corrupted labels with AUROC of 84.3–100.0% across the tested datasets and corruption levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-averaged input loss curvature can identify synthetically mislabeled training examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Toy-example curvature rises early and decreases during later overfitting and margin maximization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input loss curvature varies during training and can decline after correct classification as prediction margins increase.

record.problems: The target random-label fitting behavior is cited from prior work and not independently tested. The corruption experiments report AUROC for detecting noisy labels, not train/test errors over a full corruption sweep. The toy dynamics are shown and described but lack numerical curvature values. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated AUROC scores.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; 20 rows retained. Comparisons to FZ memorization scores and visualizations of natural high-curvature samples were excluded because they do not measure a version's named random-label fitting behavior.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error under that condition, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios and convergence rates across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit across the full corruption sweep; steadily increasing test error toward chance; retention of remaining signal. Only perfect training fit at 1% MNIST label corruption is explicitly established.

Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels and whether removing regularization harms true-label generalization. Curvature comparisons with weight decay do not establish these outcomes.
Separate learning trajectories for shared real-data patterns and noisy or random labels.

missing.what: Add a training-accuracy row: modified ResNet18 achieves 100% training accuracy on MNIST after uniformly changing 60 labels per class to incorrect classes, totaling 600 of 60,000 examples. Link to V4, state observed, restricted to its training-fit component.

record.verdict_notes: Do not interpret detection AUROC as training accuracy or infer perfect fitting throughout Table 2's corruption sweep. Fully randomized-label fitting is attributed to Zhang et al., not independently demonstrated here. The supplied manuscript identifies itself as an under-review preprint; the record's ICML publication designation is unsupported by this text.

versions.untested_parts: No fully random labeling experiment measuring training error, test error, or unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time or convergence rate against clean labels or across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The study tests label corruption for curvature-based identification, but does not report training and test error across corruption fractions or whether training accuracy stays perfect throughout the sweep.
Weight decay settings are used in curvature comparisons, but the study does not test whether regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
No experiment compares when real-label patterns and noisy or random labels are learned.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (modified versions)
rows.operation_detail: Trained to 100% training accuracy after randomly corrupting 60 labels per MNIST class, then curvature scores were examined.

conditions.value: 1% of the dataset; 60 images per class

rows.measure: Curvature of corrupted examples relative to clean examples
rows.value: Most corrupted examples had curvature scores among the highest.
rows.note: This result establishes curvature behavior after the network is trained to full memorization; it does not report the claim versions' train/test error behavior.
rows.check: The recorded measure is curvature ranking, which cannot establish any version. Preserve that finding separately from the explicitly reported 100% training accuracy, which needs a V4 row.

source_check.correct: Section 4.3 specifies weight decay of 10−4 for all models in the synthetic-corruption experiments.
source_check.problem: The condition records weight decay as not stated, although Section 4.3 specifies it.

rows.subject: 7 fully connected layer toy network
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 150 epochs with 30% noise in the training data; per-epoch curvature and losses were examined.

conditions.value: 100 points for each class, no noise
SGD, learning rate 0.1, momentum 0.9, weight decay 5e-4

rows.measure: Per-epoch curvature dynamics around training points
rows.value: Curvature increases early, then starts to decrease after overfitting takes over.
rows.note: Authors describe the trend; no numeric curvature values or clean-label comparison.
rows.check: Curvature dynamics do not establish real-label learning before noisy-label memorization. The text does not clearly identify the toy noise as label corruption; do not infer that condition.
